subject.title: Feature: temp artifact provenance + durable-path guardrails to prevent /tmp chaos

question: Should OpenClaw core own a generic temp artifact provenance and cleanup model, or should core only add runtime-critical temp-path guardrails plus a plugin/API seam for workflow-specific provenance?
rationale: The safety goal matches current priorities, but the implementation crosses storage policy, agent/tool APIs, cleanup authority, doctor/runtime guardrails, and core-versus-plugin boundaries that need maintainer intent before a safe implementation can be queued.

options.title: Core Guardrails Plus Plugin Seam
options.body: Core would handle runtime-critical temp-path checks and a minimal SQLite-backed provenance/API seam, while workflow-specific audit and janitor classification lives outside core.

options.title: Full Core Provenance Registry
options.body: Core would own classification, registry storage, durable routing, and cleanup semantics for first-class OpenClaw temp artifacts, accepting broader product and migration responsibility.

options.title: Keep Narrow Cleanup Bugs Only
options.body: Decline the broad default model and continue fixing concrete temp-path or cleanup bugs such as session temp sweeps and volatile state-dir checks separately.

recommendation.title: Core Guardrails Plus Plugin Seam
recommendation.body: Core would handle runtime-critical temp-path checks and a minimal SQLite-backed provenance/API seam, while workflow-specific audit and janitor classification lives outside core.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest combined signal on product scope, temp-boundary history, and core-versus-plugin direction among the inspected files and history.
